s: A manufacturing company runs 180 Windows and Linux servers in an on-premises VMware environment. The servers host line-of-business applications with locally attached databases. The company wants to use AWS as its disaster recovery site. The requirements are an RPO measured in seconds and an RTO of under 30 minutes. The company does not want to pay for running replica servers on AWS and wants to run non-disruptive recovery drills every quarter. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
o: Use AWS Application Migration Service to replicate the servers continuously. During a disaster, launch cutover instances and finalize the cutover.
Use AWS Backup for VMware to back up the virtual machines every hour to a backup vault in AWS. Restore the virtual machines as EC2 instances during a disaster.
Deploy AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway in cached mode for every server. Take EBS snapshots every 15 minutes and create EC2 instances from the snapshots during a disaster.

Install the AWS Replication Agent and use AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery to continuously replicate the servers into a low-cost staging area subnet. Use drill launches for quarterly tests and recovery launches during a disaster.

w.y: Elastic Disaster Recovery uses continuous block-level replication (RPO of seconds) into a cheap staging area and launches full-size recovery instances only on demand, usually within minutes. Drill launches test recovery without stopping replication, so it meets the 'LEAST operational overhead' requirement.

o.A: Application Migration Service is built for one-time migration cutovers, not for ongoing DR with drills and failback.
o.B: Hourly VM backups give an RPO of an hour, not seconds.
o.C: Snapshots every 15 minutes miss a seconds-level RPO, and converting volumes into bootable EC2 instances is manual work.
o.D: Correct: DRS gives a seconds-level RPO and a minutes-level RTO, pays only for staging resources, and supports non-disruptive drills.

d: LEAST operational overhead (RPO seconds, RTO < 30 min)
